metadata.title: Pay Per Call Masterclass - Real Time Bidding for Calls
metadata.author: Ringba
metadata.shortDescription:
The world's largest buyers of phone calls buy them programmatically, and that means they're using technology like Ringba to make decisions on which calls they're going to buy, how much they're going to pay for them, and where their calls are going to go.

Find out how Real Time Bidding for Inbound Phone Calls works and what it means for the future of Pay Per Call.

0:00:10 - What is Real-Time Bidding for Phone Calls
0:01:02 - How Real Time Bidding for Calls Works
0:02:44 - RTB for Phone Calls Flow
0:05:07 - How Call Routing Works with Real Time Bidding

Read the Lesson Transcript:
https://www.paypercallers.com/threads/real-time-bidding-for-calls.1137/

Check out the Ringba Blog Post: 
https://www.ringba.com/blog/pay-per-call/real-time-bidding-for-calls


Ringba's Pay Per Call Masterclass is the most comprehensive pay per call training course ever created. Best of all, the entire course is absolutely free.

Start Your Pay Per Call Journey: https://www.PayPerCallMasterclass.com 

----

ABOUT RINGBA:
Ringba is an inbound call tracking and analytics platform for connecting consumers with businesses. Purpose-built for performance, reliability and flexibility, Ringba provides on demand access to telecom networks in 60+ countries, intelligent call flow management and real-time analytics and reporting to performance marketers, contact centers and pay per call networks.

metadata.title: Account Setup | Ringba Call Tracking & Analytics
metadata.author: Ringba
metadata.shortDescription:
In this getting started tutorial, you will learn how to setup your Ringba account and create your first Campaign. 

HOW TO VERIFY YOUR BILLING INFORMATION

Please ensure that you upload the required documents or your service may be disrupted when we are unable to bill your card. To verify your information, click 'Verify' when prompted, or navigate to "Billing Settings" under 'Settings'.

HOW TO CREATE YOUR FIRST CAMPAIGN

Inside the Ringba Platform, all calls are routed through Campaigns.

To create a new campaign, click on "Create Campaign" under 'Campaigns'. Whenever you create Campaign, the campaign wizard will guide you through the entire setup process. 

Once you've created your campaign, you'll be taken to the 'Campaign Details' page. From here, you can install Call Tracking Tags, configure Payout Settings, manage your call routing and setup URL parameters and campaign pixels.

----------------

ABOUT RINGBA

Ringba is a global communications platform for connecting consumers with businesses. Purpose-built for performance, reliability and flexibility, Ringba provides on demand access to telecom networks in 60+ countries, intelligent call flow management and real-time analytics and reporting to performance marketers, contact centers and pay per call networks. 

No contracts or commitments. We're confident our call management platform will drastically improve your Return on Investment.

Learn more: https://www.Ringba.com
Get started for free: https://www.Ringba.com/signup
Talk to a product expert: https://Ringba.com/demo

https://twitter.com/Ringba

Learn the path to success for building a sustainable pay per call business in the performance marketing industry. 

0:00:13 - The Pay Per Call Path to Success

1:01:57 - Create Self-Serve / Micro Buyer Networks
1:03:57 - Create Your Own Brands and Assets

1:08:15 - Leverage Affiliates to Scale

metadata.title: Pay Per Call Masterclass - How Pay Per Call Networks Function
metadata.author: Ringba
metadata.shortDescription:
A Pay Per Call Network is a company or platform that manages call campaigns on behalf of advertisers and generates calls through the network of publishers.

Learn how a Pay Per Call Network operates, what they offer and how to work with them as an affiliate or advertiser.

0:00:11 - How Networks Function
0:01:09 - Potential Team Members
0:12:46 - How Networks Operate 
0:21:44 - Pros and Cons of Working with a Pay Per Call Network
0:29:45 - Getting Started with Pay Per Call Networks
0:39:42 - Network Routing Plan Example
0:44:32 - Optimizing Your Call Flow
0:46:41 - Multi-Network Routing Plan Example

Read the Episode Transcript:
https://www.paypercallers.com/threads/how-pay-per-call-networks-function.1138/

metadata.title: Pay Per Call Masterclass - How Pay Per Call Works
metadata.author: Ringba
metadata.shortDescription:
Pay Per Call is an advertising model that allows businesses to buy inbound phone calls from consumers who are interested in their products or services.

Learn how Pay Per Call works, who's involved, the technology used and what an inbound call flow looks like from start to finish. 

0:00:11 - Pay Per Call Explained
0:03:56 - Example Pay Per Call Flow from Start to Finish
0:04:12 - Advertiser Creates a Pay Per Call campaign
0:05:22 - Pay Per Call Network promotes the campaign to their Publishers.
0:06:19 - Publishers apply to the Pay Per Call campaign and receive a unique tracking number.
0:08:31 - Publishers generate inbound calls through traffic sources.
0:09:09 - Customer sees tracking numbers and clicks to call.
0:09:45 - Call is tracked and attributed to the publisher that generated the call.
0:11:03 - Customer is routed to the Advertisers
0:11:53 - Publisher receives commission for calls that meet the payout criteria for the campaign
0:13:06 - Pay Per Call Flow Diagram

Read the Lesson Transcript:
https://www.paypercallers.com/threads/how-pay-per-call-works.1134/

Check out the Ringba Blog Post:
https://www.ringba.com/blog/pay-per-call/how-pay-per-call-works


Ringba's Pay Per Call Masterclass is the most comprehensive pay per call training course ever created. Best of all, the entire course is absolutely free.

Start Your Pay Per Call Journey: https://www.PayPerCallMasterclass.com

Ringba is an inbound call tracking and analytics platform for connecting consumers with businesses. Purpose-built for performance, reliability and flexibility, Ringba provides on demand access to telecom networks in 60+ countries, intelligent call flow management and real-time analytics and reporting to performance marketers, contact centers and pay per call networks.

In this tutorial, I explain what is pay per call affiliate marketing and how to do pay per call affiliate marketing. Most people do affiliate marketing by selling products for which they collect commissions when sales are made. Other people do CPA affiliate marketing where they collect commission when users perform some action. But another great way to make money is by doing pay per call affiliate marketing. For short, it is sometimes called PPC affiliate marketing.

I offer a full affiliate marketing curse:
https://www.udemy.com/make-money-with-affiliate-marketing-earn-passive-income

Pay per call affiliate marketing can be especially effective if your traffic is mobile. Is your traffic is mobile, they already have a phone in their hands. How Agents Are Making $50,000 Per Month Only Taking Calls: http://theagentsystem.net?utm_source=yt&video=GV0ML_xytX8

The NEW Way to Buy Qualified Calls in 2026: https://youtu.be/UFWPlbDFPOg

---------------------------------------------------------------

Building a pay per call system that actually converts starts with understanding why traditional lead generation fails

Most agents waste thousands on garbage leads because they're optimizing for cost per lead instead of cost per enrolled customer

That one metric shift changes everything

I'm walking you through the complete call generation framework I built after managing over $100 million in ad spend across insurance and home services

This system has five core components that turn cold traffic into consumer-initiated inbound calls converting at 25-30% instead of the industry standard 2-3%

You'll learn how high-intent ad campaigns on Google, Facebook, and YouTube create qualified prospects who actually want to talk to you

I'm also covering why consumer-initiated calls have zero TCPA liability compared to cold outreach, and how intelligent call routing with IVR systems ensures the right agent answers every call at the right time

The call intelligence layer tracks which campaigns drive real enrollments, not just clicks. Plus, the implementation strategy gets most teams live and taking calls within minutes

Agents making this shift are seeing 10-20x production increases. Lead quality industry-wide has collapsed while TCPA enforcement is ramping up

If you're still buying aged lead lists or cold calling Facebook forms, you're competing with last decade's playbook

This PRiMe Calls training shows licensed agents how buffer times work and how to use those first seconds of an inbound call.

Every call type has a buffer, which is the time before a call becomes billable. This walkthrough covers what happens during the buffer, how to stay on the call the right way, and what to avoid so you follow the process you agreed to when your campaign went live.

Get started at primecalls.io

[www.tiktok.com/@primecalls.io](https://www.tiktok.com/@primecalls.io)
[www.instagram.com/primecalls.io](https://www.instagram.com/primecalls.io/)

For licensed agents only. Results vary.

course of ten to fifteen years they go to the office so always demonstrate lifetime value especially if the business owner is objecting to netting zero on the initial purchase I like to say in the likely case you don't profit on the initial purchase you're essentially getting lifetime customers for free and I don't know about you but I'd take free customers all day so pretty much everything that I just said is a rambling way of saying make sure that you can get a good profit margin while still selling the call at a value that makes sense for the customer lastly you're gonna have to eventually be doing outreach to get in contact with these companies to sell so might as well make sure right away it will be semi easy to get in contact with decision-makers either through email or phone I made this mistake assuming urgent care clinics would be a good industry to go into and then realize it's very difficult to get in contact with the decision-maker at those companies really the best way in this niche would have been to go to networking events in the industry I'm not gonna say it's impossible to get in contact with the decision maker in any industries but I'm sure you can think of a few that may require more creativity when you may or may not want to expend that energy as mentioned there's nothing like just testing an ad to see how it performs for forty to fifty dollars you can at least get a sense of what you're dealing with for this reason I use affiliate networks not for profit but to test ideas and verticals as fast as possible but what about the verticals that aren't offered by affiliate networks well I've come up with a pretty cool solution for that simply route a campaign to a local business no need to apply to a network get approved for an offer or even sell client data is what we want so why not just send some leads to a business and see how the campaign performs hell you could even go to the business after and show them the data for the leads you sent them and see if they want to become a client now I'm not sure what the legalities are behind this specifically the call recording aspect of it so that being said I'm not a lawyer and has suggest doing your own due diligence specifically when it comes to call recording however I don't see any moral issues with sending some customers to a business unbeknownst it's essentially the same as telling people you like their company and that they should use them you may want to leave out the call recording portion of it though in the discussion with the client as this might have more of a negative effect than a positive upside so yeah it's as simple as setting up a local campaign and routing calls to the phone number of a company in the area if an industry has high mobile usage but you're unsure about the intent might as well target all the services would call only and the data will show you which specific ones target for call only ads you may waste some money on useless clicks but this is all data and it's all information so it's worth it if you're fairly certain only a few keywords are going to work your emergency terms for example then go ahead and just set up a campaign with these only keep in mind you will likely have to make adjustments to the campaign in order to get significant enough data just like you would do with an affiliate campaign on a national level so with some data coming in you'll now have some information to make a solid judgment of whether to go into an industry as well as an idea of what the charge for leads you also have initial data for which you can use in sales processes as proof of concept here are some things to pay attention to to determine a good industry first is the cost per call low relative to what you would charge a client are your margins going to work with this are the impressions and call volume high enough to justify going into the industry is there a high phone through rate if you see a lot of clicks turning in the phone calls this is always a good sign what are the search terms like so are there a lot of high intent searches are there a lot of unforeseen negative keywords that might harm your cost per call also listen to call recordings to see if people are making appointments with the company this is just validation that that people have high intent and will call a call only add-in instead of appointment so these are all the main things that I look for when moving into a specific niche in looking to do pay per call model I think that covers just about everything that I found in the past eight the ten months that I've been doing this I'm sure there's stuff that I may have missed and I'm sure everything is not perfect so if you have anything to add put those in the comments metadata.title: Inbound Call Standards & Expectations | Integrity Connect x Ringba Training
metadata.author: FFL Success Zone | Integrity Connect Inbounds
metadata.shortDescription:
This training covers the official standards and expectations for inbound Final Expense calls on the Integrity Connect platform, built in partnership with Ringba.
In this session, we’re joined by Shanti Beaurline, Director of Business Development & Revenue Growth at Ringba, to explain how inbound call traffic is generated, how publishers and media buyers operate, and why agent behavior directly impacts call quality, volume, and profitability.
This video is part of the Integrity Connect Boot Camp and is also used as remedial training for agents who have been temporarily paused or are struggling with performance.
You’ll learn:

How Ringba inbound calls are generated through paid media (Meta, YouTube, search, CTV)
Why RPC (Revenue Per Call) is the most important metric on the platform
The minimum standards agents must meet to remain active
Why taking calls past 90 seconds improves call quality over time
How agent behavior affects publisher traffic and ad quality
What happens when agents cherry‑pick, rush quotes, or beat the buzzer
Examples of good vs bad inbound calls
Why scripts matter and what happens when agents wing it
What behaviors result in temporary pause or permanent removal
How predictive routing rewards agents with higher RPCs
Why inbound calls are not “free benefits” and how to handle that objection properly
Why inbound calls still require real insurance sales skills

This training is designed to protect the platform, protect publishers, and most importantly, help agents become profitable long‑term by handling inbound calls the right way.
If you want consistent call flow, better quality prospects, and higher income from inbound calls, these standards are not optional—they are the path to winning.

metadata.title: Interactive Voice Response | Ringba Call Tracking & Analytics
metadata.author: Ringba
metadata.shortDescription:
Learn everything you need to know about creating, configuring and using Interactive Voice Response with Ringba.

An IVR or “Interactive-Voice-Response” is an automated system for qualifying callers with prompts and routing them to a destination based on their responses. Ringba’s intuitive drag-and-drop IVR Builder and flexible rules-based routing engine makes it easy to design and track and control your traffic, call flow and customer experience.

Interactive Voice Response makes it easy to configure caller prompts for qualifying and routing your calls exactly where they need to go in real-time. The IVR Builder also features whisper messaging, automatic text-to-speech in 15+ languages, the ability to upload custom IVR audio files and more while the reporting suite provides detailed analytics abouts how your caller interacted with your IVR.

CREATING AN IVR

Step 1) Setup Routing Plan

To setup a Routing Plan, navigate to “Routing Plans” from the main Dashboard and click on “Create Routing Plan”.

Give your Routing Plan a “Name” and click on “Create” to begin adding destinations. Setup your Targets / Groups and configure their settings like Weight and Priority. Click on “Close” and your Routing Plan settings will be saved automatically.

Step 2) Build an IVR Tree

Your next step is to build your IVR Tree. Navigate to IVRs from the main menu and select “Create IVR Tree”. 

At the top of the IVR builder, you can name your IVR, save your configuration and expand or collapse your nodes for a high-level overview of your IVR. Drag-and-drop Nodes are used to build your IVR trees. You can add your first Node by dragging the node onto the workspace.

Step 3) Route to a Campaign

Now it’s time to put it our IVR to work by attaching it to a campaign.

To switch a campaign from Standard Routing to IVR Routing, navigate to “Manage Campaigns” under “Campaigns” from the main Dashboard. Find the Campaign and click into the “Campaign Details” page.

Next, scroll down to “Call Routing”. Click on “IVR” and select your IVR Tree from the dropdown menu. Your Routing Settings for the Campaign will be updated and saved automatically.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

"How do I make changes or edit an IVR Tree?"
To make changes to your IVR, navigate to “Manage IVR Trees” under ‘IVR’ and click “Edit IVR”.

"Why can’t I save my IVR Tree?"
Your IVR Tree must meet validation criteria before you can save it for use in a Campaign. Nodes causing validation errors will be marked with a red counter beside the Node Name. Hover over the counter to learn more about the validation error.

"How do I make changes or edit an IVR Tree?"
To make changes to your IVR, navigate to “Manage IVR Trees” under ‘IVR’ and click “Edit IVR”.

"Can I use the same IVR Tree for multiple Campaigns?"
Of course! IVR was built to be flexible, dynamic and valuable for any and every use case.

"What IVR data is available in the Call Log?"
If a call is routed through an IVR Tree, the Call Log will report on the caller’s; IVR Tree and Enter / Exit Nodes. 


----------------

Ringba is a global communications platform for connecting consumers with businesses. Purpose-built for performance, reliability and flexibility, Ringba provides on demand access to telecom networks in 60+ countries, intelligent call flow management and real-time analytics and reporting to performance marketers, contact centers and pay per call networks.

The 10 best call center software for insurance are JustCall, Genesys Cloud, Talkdesk, NiCE CXone, Zoom Contact Center, Convoso, Readymode, Ringba, Ricochet360 and Ringy, ranked on two questions: can it record, find and keep a sales call, and what does one agent seat cost? JustCall ranks first, with every call recorded from $29 a seat billed annually.

The test every call center software for insurance has to pass
• Medicare marketing rules say plans and the agents who sell for them record sales calls in full and keep them for six years, as audio for at least the first three. Can the software record every call, find it again and keep it that long?
• What does one agent seat cost at the published price and billing term?

The 10 best call center software for insurance, ranked
1. JustCall. Every call is recorded from the first plan, and AI Transcription writes a summary with action items that syncs to your CRM. A visual multi-level IVR routes callers by skill or to the contact owner in the CRM. Supervisors listen, whisper or barge in, and AI Call Scoring grades each conversation. SOC 2 Type II, with Salesforce among 70+ native integrations. From $29 a seat billed annually, skills-based routing at $49, 14-day free trial. Claro Insurance reached a connection rate above 70% with full visibility into its bilingual IVR.
2. Genesys Cloud. A full contact center suite with outbound campaigns and a speech IVR on the first plan. Voice and digital interaction recording plus screen recording come standard. $75 a user a month billed annually; QA and compliance tools at $115.
3. Talkdesk. Your team sets the recording and retention rules, and recordings stay on the Talkdesk cloud or on your own storage. The voice plan is $105 a user a month, and the industry edition is $225.
4. NiCE CXone. The entry Omnichannel Suite bundles voice, routing, call recording and compliance tools from one vendor. $110 an agent a month; outbound dialing is sold as an add-on.
5. Zoom Contact Center. A flow editor for the IVR, real-time transcription, PII redaction and encryption at rest on the first plan, $69 a user billed annually. Outbound dialers from $99.
6. Convoso. An outbound dialer that routes insurance leads by state and enforces TCPA and state calling rules, with call recordings kept in secure storage. Annual plans quoted by sales, no free trial; Salesforce integration listed as coming soon.
7. Readymode. A high-volume dialer for Medicare insurance teams that records every call or only the ones you choose. $199 a license a month billed annually on Starter, $249 on iQ for teams of five or more; inbound minutes are billed separately.
8. Ringba. Tracks and routes inbound calls from paid ads and pay-per-call campaigns, with an IVR builder to screen callers. $127 a month billed annually; call recording is 1 cent a minute and transcription 4 cents a minute.
9. Ricochet360. A calling CRM with an insurance setup that includes call recording, monitoring and DNC scrubbing, plus IVR routing on every plan. $20 a user billed annually, the lowest seat here, with 500 minutes a month.
10. Ringy. An insurance CRM with call recording, local caller ID and 1,000 outbound minutes and texts in the base price, plus a free trial. $119 a month; the power dialer adds $70 for a total of $189.

metadata.shortDescription:
If you’re a plumber and you’re tired of relying on word-of-mouth or hoping someone finds your number on Google, this video is for you. In this comprehensive guide, we break down a modern lead generation system specifically designed for plumbing companies that want consistent, high-quality leads without burning money on bad ads or outdated tactics.

You’ll learn how to combine platforms like Google Local Services Ads (LSA), Meta Ads, Local SEO, and even direct mail into a synchronized strategy that brings you leads every day. Whether you’re doing residential plumbing, emergency repairs, or commercial jobs, this system shows you how to attract the right kind of customer—the ones who are ready to book and willing to pay.

We also explain how to track every step of your pipeline, use automations like email and SMS follow-ups, and avoid common mistakes that drain your marketing budget. This isn’t theory—this is based on real campaigns we’ve run for contractors across the U.S., with data to back it up.

If you’re serious about scaling your plumbing business, getting better clients, and finally building a predictable way to grow month after month, this video is your starting point. Watch now and learn how to turn your business into a lead-generating machine that works for you—even while you’re out on the job.

Here’s the deal:

📌 If your service is urgent (roof leaks, burst pipes, no AC)… Google and LSA will feed your crew.
📌 If your service is visual, emotional, or aspirational (remodeling, painting, windows, flooring)… Meta and YouTube are your goldmine.
📌 And if you don’t know which category you fall into?

You’re probably burning money right now without even knowing it.

🎯 Want a marketing system built specifically for your trade that actually gets results?

👉 Book a Free Demo Call: https://contractormarketingpros.net/calendar

Contractor Marketing Pros

We help contractors get found online, generate quality leads, and dominate their local markets.

Let’s build your machine.

🔔 Subscribe for more no-fluff contractor marketing content every week.

 📞 Questions? Drop them in the comments or reach out directly.

Thanks for watching. Now let’s go get some leads. 💥

metadata.shortDescription:
If you're a new or part-time final expense insurance agent, choosing the right lead source can make a big difference in your sales results. In this video, learn how live transfer leads work, what they cost, and how to decide which lead strategy makes sense for your business.

📞 NEED MORE FINAL EXPENSE CALLING OPPORTUNITIES?

BigDials offers unlimited outbound final expense leads with a predictive dialer, plus inbound call solutions for agents looking to grow their production.

Learn more:

https://bigdials.com/

🚀 LOOKING TO JOIN A FINAL EXPENSE AGENCY?

Gold Standard Coverage provides final expense agents with training, support, and access to our lead and dialing program.

Register for our next agency overview to learn more:

https://goldstandardcoverage.com/watch


Most agents jump into Facebook leads too early and get burned because they can't keep up with speed-to-lead. Live transfers can solve that problem—but they come with their own risks.

Here's what you'll learn:

- What live transfers actually are (TV vs outbound)
- Real cost per sale for beginners vs experienced agents
- Why part-time agents struggle with Facebook leads
- When live transfers make sense (and when they don't)
- The best way to structure your first 30–60 days in insurance

If you're serious about getting your first few sales and building momentum, this is the strategy I recommend based on real-world results.

Now, his goal is to help train, mentor and motivate insurance agents all over the world to operate at their highest level. metadata.title: Inbound vs Outbound Calls: What's the Difference?
metadata.author: Global Call Forwarding
metadata.shortDescription:
Inbound and outbound calls serve different purposes and thus require different approaches. 

So, to properly manage your business’ calls, it’s important to understand the difference between inbound vs outbound calls.

Inbound calls are those traveling to your business, meaning you wait for customers to contact you. 

As such, these types of calls typically involve questions, troubleshooting, concerns, or complaints from customers and prospects.

On the other hand, outbound calls are those traveling from your business, meaning your teams place the calls. 

And these calls usually involve prospecting, upselling, offering upgrades or renewals, and promotions. 

In this video, we will dig deeper into the differences between inbound vs outbound calls. And we’ll cover the best features and call center software for each call type. This way, you can choose the best tech to support your business needs and goals. 

A reliable VoIP provider, like Global Call Forwarding, offers your business access to advanced call features and tools. So, you can create a phone system that fits your needs. 

To learn more about our services and how we can support your business goals, speak to our experts at +1 (561) 908-6171 or visit us online.

Using concurrency and capping to make
routing decisions is crucial to load
balancing your calls and ensuring you
never drop the ball or lose a potential
conversion.
Concurrency is the number of
simultaneous calls that a buyer can
receive or is receiving at one time. By
configuring concurrency caps, you can
intelligently determine if all the
agents in a buyer's call center are busy
and then automatically reroute your call
flow to a buyer that can accept them.
Capping or caps, short for capacity, is
the amount of call traffic a buyer is
willing to accept. When working with
call buyers, they often set a limit on
how many calls they're willing to buy
from you on a daily, weekly, or monthly
basis. If you were to send them more
calls after you've already hit your
buyer's cap, they won't pay you for
them. By configuring capacity in your
routing plans, you can effortlessly stop
sending calls to buyers whose caps you
already hit and reroute your call flow
to the call buyers that are hungry for
them. This tool can also be used to
protect you when working with new buyers
by limiting the amount of money they owe
you. For instance, if you want to limit
your financial exposure to a new buyer,
you can cap them at $2,000 for the first
2 weeks to make sure they pay before
sending them any more calls. Zip code
routing is crucial to successful paper
call campaigns. Geographic routing
simply means routing phone calls by the
geographic location of the caller.
Though it doesn't necessarily matter
where the call center is, what does
matter in campaigns that are geo routed
is where the callers are calling from.
Most call tracking platforms will only
route by area code, but this is a flawed
method. Why? Because approximately 35%
of all people have a different area code
than where they're located. If someone
calls from a 248 area code, but doesn't
live in Michigan, then they'll be
connected to the wrong call center.
If you use area code-based geo routing,
you're leaving a lot of money on the
table because if 35% of area codes are
wrong, that means that approximately 35%
of the time, based on what's going on
with your call flow, there's a chance
that you're not getting paid for a phone
call where someone actually wants to buy
insurance or whatever the product is,
but they can't because of licensing. The
best, most successful marketers are
data-driven. So, why should pay-per-call
be any different? Ringba gives you full
control over the data route,
specifically by where a user is
physically located, not by their area
code. Because of Ringba's number pool
technology, they're able to figure out
the actual zip code, city, state,
country, latitude, and longitude, if you
want, of where a caller is actually
coming from. Then, inside Ringba's
platform, you can actually make routing
decisions with that information.
Make routing decisions, load balance
your calls, and ensure you never drop a
call or lose out on a potential
conversion with Ringba's call tracking
software.

to optimize your paper call routing.
SIP routing means using voice over IP
instead of a traditional phone number to
connect directly to your buyer's contact
center software. This results in faster
connection times, better voice quality,
plus the ability to seamlessly pass data
in the SIP header, which all result in
better conversion rates for your calls.
If the buyers have the capability to
accept calls via SIP, you should
absolutely take advantage of this
optimization tactic to get better
results. Handling busy buyers and
non-answered calls are a breeze when
you're using your own call tracking
software like Ringba. If your buyer
doesn't answer the phone or the call is
busy, Ringba will automatically reroute
the phone call to another buyer as many
times as it takes to make sure the call
is connected. Unfortunately, if you're a
media buyer or a publisher relying on a
network's tracking, you're out of luck.
Rerouting these types of calls in real
time is essential to eliminating wasted
ad spend, improving conversion rates,
and maximizing the value of every call
you generate.
Routing calls based on hours of
operation is really simple, but you'd be
surprised how often it's overlooked. And
when something is overlooked in a paper
call campaign, that's where money starts
going down the drain.
When configuring your routing plan and
setting up your buyer's targets, make
sure that you include their hours of
operation, including lunch time and
breaks. Sending calls to a contact
center when everyone is away from their
desk, eating lunch means that your calls
will get dropped or go to voicemail. And
that also means you, more than likely,
won't be paid for the call. The good
news is that it's really simple to
manage. Simply request the hours of
operation from your buyer and adjust
your routing plans, then target
accordingly. In most cases, buyers will
not pay you for duplicate calls, which
means you're leaving lots of money on
the floor by not remonetizing your
duplicate calls and routing them to a
new buyer. If you're working with a
network, they're most likely going to
sell those duplicate calls to multiple
parties on the back end, but they're
only going to pay you once per caller.

profits, but by using your own call
tracking software like Ringba, you can
essentially take away the ability for a

your dime. You can take that margin away

metadata.title: How Calls Are Tracked and Routed | Pay-Per-Call Masterclass
metadata.author: TrackDrive
metadata.shortDescription:
From the ad to the answered phone: what happens in the seconds in between.

This episode follows a single phone call from the moment a consumer sees an ad to the moment a person answers, in five steps. It covers tracking numbers and how the platform knows where a call came from, routing and filters that decide who gets the call, and ping/post, where buyers bid for a call in real time. It closes with what is logged after the call connects: the record everyone relies on to decide which calls qualified.

0:26 What this episode covers
0:43 Dial, identify, filter
2:08 Route
3:09 Record
3:40 Three ideas to take with you
4:27 Up next

Next episode: Ep 4 · Setting Up a Campaign https://youtu.be/ncatAE6wf_0

What a paid phone call is, why advertisers value calls so highly, and how a call compares with a click or a lead.

Join our Pest Control Pay-Per-Call webinar and learn how affiliates and media buyers can generate high-quality inbound calls for local pest control services across the US.

📅 Thursday, July 2nd at 1:00 PM EST

Speakers:
• Alex Shkarupa — VP of Operations, Marketcall https://t.me/alexshkarupa
• Shaggad Mannan — Affiliate Manager, Marketcall https://t.me/shaggad_marketcall

• How the Pest Control Pay-Per-Call model works in competitive local markets

• Proven ad angles and funnels currently working in pest control
• Compliance rules to keep campaigns stable and scalable

The slides from the webinar: https://tools.marketcall.com/mastermind/

Check us out here: https://www.marketcall.com/

Join our TG-channels to stay updated:
https://t.me/marketcall_com

metadata.author: Evocalize
metadata.shortDescription:
Matthew Marx, CEO of Evocalize, and Eric Troutman, TCPA attorney at Troutman & Amin, dive into the FCC's latest rule changes requiring explicit one-to-one consent for lead generation. 

Discover how these new rules mandate clear consumer consent before capturing lead information and the necessity of enumerating specific providers.

This video is 3 of an 11-part series diving into the FCC's recent changes to lead generation practices. 

Check out the full playlist here: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLCPB_1eSg1hKdhHccKT1ZYUcPkH0G_MY1

#LeadGeneration #ConsumerSpam #AggressiveMarketing #FCCRegulations #LeadAggregation #FCC #TCPA #LeadGen

Unlock the secrets of modern lead generation with ActiveProspect and Boberdoo in this exclusive webinar, designed to optimize your lead gen strategy while ensuring compliance with the FCC’s updated TCPA regulations. - Building a comprehensive consent checklist
- Understanding the nuances of exclusive vs. shared leads

metadata.title: 2024 TCPA Updates & Lead Generation Compliance
metadata.author: Mike Fitzpatrick
metadata.shortDescription:
Get the latest insights into the 2024 Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) updates and discover how to keep your lead generation fully compliant. In this in-depth Masterclass, we’ll cover everything from the recent changes to the TCPA, best practices for collecting valid consent, and the potential fines you could face if you don’t comply.

What You’ll Learn:

Key TCPA changes affecting lead generation in 2024
How to capture valid consent (and what “blanket” consent no longer means)
Real-world examples of TCPA violations and fines
Strategies for record-keeping and verifying lead sources
Top questions to ask your vendors to ensure compliance
Best practices to avoid class action lawsuits or FCC enforcement

2:45 - A2P Messaging: What You Need to Know – Carriers are cracking down!
5:10 - Best Practices for Lead Generation & Texting – Avoid getting flagged as spam.

8:00 - Marketing Smarter, Not Riskier – The importance of fresh, exclusive leads.

metadata.title: FCC SERIES: EPISODE 11 - Actionable strategies for TCPA-compliant texting and lead gen
metadata.author: ActiveProspect, Inc.
metadata.shortDescription:
Text with compliance; text with confidence



As January 2025 approaches, the FCC is set to implement a transformative update to the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA). Join us for this webinar as we offer a comprehensive exploration of the new TCPA regulations and practical guidance for adapting your text message marketing strategies. Whether you are a buyer or a seller in the lead-gen or marketing industries, understanding these changes is crucial to maintaining compliance and optimizing your texting and calling outreach operations.

  •  Strategic adaptations for marketers: Discover strategies to redesign your lead-generation models to comply with the future of the TCPA.
  •  Technological requirements for compliance: Identify the necessary technology solutions to effectively capture and document consent across all marketing channels and how to align your entire company.
  •  Vendor management and compliance: Understand the importance of vetting vendors and their agreements to ensure they are TCPA-compliant.
  •  Avoiding pitfalls with carriers and texting consent: Learn how to navigate carrier requirements and avoid common SMS mistakes that could lead to non-compliance or service disruptions.
  •  Proactive compliance: Manage risks by monitoring opt-out rates, updating lead forms for consent verification, limiting daily message volumes, avoiding irrelevant phone numbers, and segmenting campaigns to target specific audiences effectively.

This webinar is ideal for marketers, compliance officers, and anyone involved in lead generation or digital marketing who needs help preparing for the TCPA's new updates.

metadata.author: ActiveProspect, Inc.
metadata.shortDescription:
Join ActiveProspect's Mike Peronto with Bryan Behan from Socius Marketing and Kristen McCormick from Hatch.

Whether you are a buyer or a seller in the lead-gen or marketing industries, understanding these changes is crucial to maintaining compliance and optimizing your texting and calling outreach operations.

- Strategic adaptations for marketers
- Technological requirements for compliance
- Vendor management and compliance
- Avoiding pitfalls with carriers and texting consent
- Proactive compliance

metadata.title: Summary of the New TCPA Rules Regarding Third Party Affiliate Leads Effective January 27, 2025
metadata.author: Pitchit
metadata.shortDescription:
Short summary of the new TCPA rules, aka the Lead Generator Rule, going live on January 27, 2025.

In this video, we walk through the use case of a buyer and seller arrangement where a 3rd party affiliate "seller" captures prior express written consent from a lead, and then transfers that consent to contact over to a "buyer" in exchange for payment.

This review was prepared by Pitchit and our legal partner Rikka Law on behalf of our clients, vendors, investors, and partners to make sure everyone using the Pitchit platform is informed on new TCPA laws.

Visit our website to see the full TCPA compliance guide that we use in this video: https://www.pitchit.ai/tcpa-compliance

segments.text: Welcome back to Paper-Call University.
Today, we're going to focus on one of
the most important players in the entire
Paper-Call industry, the publisher.
Publishers are the people and companies
that create the opportunities. They
generate traffic, turn consumer intent
into phone calls, and ultimately create
something that buyers are willing to pay
for. But here's what most people don't
understand when they first get into
Paper-Call. Generating a call is only
one part of the business. You need the
right traffic, the right campaigns, the
right tracking, the right buyers, and
you need to understand the economics
behind every call you generate. In this
episode, I'm going to show you exactly
how the publisher side works, how
publishers make money, and how you can
start building digital assets that
generate calls and revenue. So where do
publishers actually get these calls?
There isn't just one traffic source.
A publisher might generate calls from
Google Ads, SEO, local websites, Google
Business Profiles, social media,
directories, native advertising, email,
or other forms of digital marketing.
Some publishers buy traffic and generate
calls immediately. Others build websites
and digital assets that can generate
organic calls month after month. And
larger publishers may use several
different traffic sources at the same
time.
But here's something extremely
important. Not all traffic is treated
equally. A buyer may love calls coming
from Google search, but refuse calls
coming from another source.
That's why, as a publisher, you need to
know exactly where every call came from.
Later in this episode, I'll show you why
separating and tracking your traffic
sources can protect your campaigns and
your entire Paper-Call business.
Now, here's something important to
understand. A publisher's real job isn't
simply to make a phone ring. The goal is
to generate real consumer intent.
Think about the difference. Someone
randomly calling a roofing company isn't
necessarily valuable.
But a homeowner who searched for roof
replacement, found your website, and
called because they actually need a new
roof, that's intent. And that's what
buyers are really paying for. The
stronger the intent, the more valuable
that opportunity can become.
This is why traffic quality matters so
much in pay per call. You can generate a
thousand calls, but if the callers
aren't genuinely interested in the
service, those calls aren't going to
create much value. On the other hand, a
smaller number of high intent calls can
generate significant revenue.
So as a publisher, don't think only
about how many calls can I generate,
think about where did the consumer come
from? What were they looking for? And
how strong was their intent when they
picked up the phone? Because ultimately,
that's what determines the quality and
the value of the traffic you're
generating. Now let's talk about
something that can make or break a
publisher, traffic source quality.
Buyers don't only care that the phone
rang, they care about how that customer

metadata.shortDescription:
What if you could open one marketplace, choose the exact type of lead you want, and start buying leads in real time?
In Pay Per Call University Episode 19, I introduce Lead Exchange™ inside ProAxis.ai — a marketplace designed to give buyers access to lead inventory across different industries, campaigns, locations, and lead types.
We cover how buyers can search and filter available inventory, see lead details before purchasing, choose the leads that fit their business, and have purchased leads organized directly inside their ProAxis.ai account.
You'll learn how Lead Exchange can give you access to:
- 🔥 Fresh & real-time leads
- 🎯 Leads by niche and campaign
- 📍 Geographic targeting
- 👑 Exclusive leads
- 👥 Shared leads
- ♻️ Recovered leads
- 📋 Lead-form opportunities
- 📞 Call opportunities
- 🧠 Intent-based lead opportunities
- ⚡ Inventory that can be purchased as it becomes available
But purchasing the lead is only the beginning.
Once the lead enters ProAxis.ai, you can use it across the rest of the platform — including AI outbound calling, email, SMS, automations, follow-up workflows, live transfers, and appointment booking.

Find the right leads → Buy them → Activate them → Generate calls, appointments & customers.
This is another piece of the complete performance marketing ecosystem we're building inside ProAxis.ai.

metadata.title: How to Generate Pay Per Call Traffic That Converts | Paid, Organic & Owned Traffic | Episode 13
metadata.author: ExclusiveLiveCall
metadata.shortDescription:
How do successful Pay Per Call publishers actually generate calls?
In Episode 13 of Pay Per Call University, we break down the major traffic sources you can use to generate Pay Per Call traffic — from paid advertising to organic traffic and digital assets you can build and own.
We cover Microsoft Ads and paid search, Facebook and Meta Ads, Messenger, Facebook Pages and Groups, TikTok, native advertising, websites, SEO, Google Business Profiles, AEO and AI search, organic content, broadcast messaging, radio and offline traffic.
But generating traffic is only half the equation.
You'll also learn how to think about the economics:
Traffic Cost → Calls → Qualified/Billable Calls → Revenue → Profit
We explain why every traffic source should be tracked separately using dedicated tracking numbers, Source IDs and SubAffiliate IDs, so you can see exactly which sources are profitable and which are losing money.
You'll also learn the difference between rented traffic and owned assets — and why building websites, content, audiences, communities and other legitimate digital properties can create long-term value instead of depending entirely on advertising spend.
Most importantly, this episode prepares us for the next major chapter of Pay Per Call University.
We're going beyond Pay Per Call and entering the larger world of Performance Marketing — including leads, intent data, visitor technology, lead enrichment, AI outbound calling, workflow automation, appointments, actions and more.
In Episode 14: What Is Performance Marketing? — Stop Paying for Advertising. Start Paying for Results.

metadata.title: How I Pay Publishers in Pay Per Call (net terms)
metadata.author: ceohec
metadata.shortDescription:
👉 Learn how net terms work so you never front your own cash to pay publishers

📞 Want help building your brokerage? Watch this VSL: https://middlemanmafia.io/?cx=xmVETW2

📆Book a call: https://middlemanmafia.io/apply?cx=K15G7jD

In this video: I explain weekly net 7 and net 3 terms with publishers and buyers, why your buyers should always pay up front, and how to line up terms so the buyer's money clears before your publisher invoice is due. Then I show a real week of billable calls inside Retreaver. For pay per call brokers setting up their first deals.

⏱️ Chapters
00:00 What net terms are
01:10 Why buyers pay up front
02:53 Scenario 1: buyer pays up front
05:16 Scenario 2: net terms on both sides
06:47 Real example inside Retreaver
08:01 Final advice on terms
08:55 Free training + next steps

🛠️ Resources
Call tracking I use: https://app.inboundx.io/r/ceohec
Related: How To Set Up Retreaver (Pay Per Call): https://youtu.be/RWVdTqjVYE8

Who I am:
Licensed insurance agent since 2022. I started by buying leads with my mom's credit card, learned to run my own ads, and now run AgentCalls, a pay per call brokerage selling calls and leads to insurance agents. Through Middleman Mafia I teach people how to build their own pay per call business

📲 Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/ceohec
💬 Telegram: https://t.me/theceohec

Results vary. Nothing here is a guarantee of income. Figures mentioned are my own or my students' and aren't typical.

What is actually working in Pay Per Call in 2026?

In episode three of Behind The Ads, Guido Silbert sits down with Alex Shkarupa, VP of Operations at Marketcall, a leading Pay Per Call affiliate network with ten years in the space.

Try AdPlexity Social: https://adplexity.io

We cover how Marketcall runs an in-house media buying team alongside their affiliate network, why 90% of their creatives are now AI-generated, the quiz and chatbot funnels that convert across debt, auto insurance, and home services, and the underpriced traffic sources most Pay Per Call affiliates have never tested — including in-app traffic at one cent CPC and Connected TV at ten to twenty dollar CPMs.

Alex also shares how he is building AI research systems on top of the AdPlexity Social API and MCP to analyze hundreds of ads at once and produce competitive intelligence reports no human analyst could match at that speed.

About Behind The Ads:

Behind The Ads is the podcast for performance marketers who want to hear what is actually working, from the operators running the campaigns. Hosted by Guido Silbert at AdPlexity. New episodes drop regularly.

metadata.title: Performance Marketing, Pay Per Call & Media Brokering with Palmer McColl | EDM Lead Network
metadata.author: EDM Lead Network
metadata.shortDescription:
CEO of EDM Lead Network, 𝐌𝐫. 𝐉𝐚𝐦𝐚𝐥 𝐄𝐧𝐠𝐥𝐢𝐬𝐡, sat down with EDM Lead Network Media Broker, Palmer McColl at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas for a conversation on performance marketing, media brokering, pay per call, traffic offers, and growth in the industry.

Mr. Palmer McColl talks about how he got started in lead generation, how he entered the performance marketing space, and what his journey has looked like since joining EDM Lead Network as a media broker.

The discussion covers the realities of building in this space, from publisher and advertiser relationships to communication, compliance, networking, campaign management, and the difference between short-term deals and long-term partnerships.

Palmer also opens up about his early lessons, first conference experience, and his vision for growth in 2026, including his goal of reaching $50,000 per day in revenue.

This podcast gives a clear look into the mindset, work ethic, and business model behind EDM Lead Network and the opportunities available in performance marketing for those who are ready to learn, build relationships, and execute.

Chapters
00:00 – 02:13: Introduction and Palmer McColl’s background in marketing
02:14 – 06:26: How Palmer discovered EDM Lead Network and entered media brokering
06:27 – 09:28: Getting started at EDM and early revenue growth
09:29 – 12:13: First industry conference experience and networking lessons
12:14 – 18:24: Entrepreneurial beginnings, e-commerce ventures, and learning marketing
18:25 – 23:17: Understanding performance marketing, campaign management, and payment terms
23:18 – 30:19: Vetting publishers, compliance, and avoiding bad business partners
30:20 – 36:25: Long-term partnerships, vertical opportunities, and industry exposure
36:26 – 45:00: The art of dealmaking, networking, and team collaboration at EDM
45:01 – 50:57: Growth mindset, industry opportunities, and Palmer’s $50K/day revenue goal
50:58 – 54:50 Education, industry insights, and closing thoughts
#EDMLeadNetwork #PerformanceMarketing #PayPerCall #LeadGeneration #MediaBroker #AffiliateMarketing

metadata.shortDescription:
Rules that protect consumers and keep your campaigns running. General education, not legal advice.

This episode is general education, not legal advice: rules differ by state and by industry and change often, so confirm current requirements with qualified counsel or your compliance team before you launch. It covers four areas: consent for calls and texts, call recording disclosures, do-not-call lists and suppressions, and state and industry rules. It ends with who is responsible for compliance when you work through a network and when you work directly.

0:43 What this episode covers
1:04 Consent for calls and texts
1:53 Call recording
2:18 Do-not-call and suppressions
2:39 State and industry rules
3:04 A word on responsibility
3:40 Three habits to take with you
4:30 Up next

Masterclass. Episode seven, compliance
essentials.
First, I want to start with one
important note. This episode is general
education. It is not legal advice and
rules differ by state and by industry
and they change often. So please confirm
the current requirements with qualified
counsel or your compliance team before
you launch anything. Compliance matters
to everyone in this business. The rules
exist to protect consumers and following
them is also what keeps campaigns
running.

campaigns, lost partners, and very

disclosures, do not call lists, and
state and industry rules.
The goal here is to help you know which
questions to ask and to build good
habits with every setup. Know the rules
before you launch.
Here are the four areas, one at a time.
First, consent for calls and texts. In
PaperCall, the consumer usually makes
the call to you, which is a very
different situation from you calling
them.
But many campaigns involve outbound
follow-up, like calling or texting a
person who filled out a form.
When that happens, the person generally
needs to have given documented consent
and that consent should name the
specific business that will contact
them.
Vague wording like our partners can be a
real problem.
I also want to flag that the rules for
calls and texts, including how a person
can withdraw their consent, have been
changing. So don't rely on what you
learned a few years ago. Confirm the
current version with your counsel.
Second, call recording.
Some states require every person on the
call to agree to a
not just one.
Because a call can cross state lines,
the safe habit is to play a clear, short
disclosure at the start of the call,
something like this.
This call may be recorded for quality
and training purposes. It's a small step
that can prevent a very large problem.
Third, do not call and suppressions.
There are national and state do not call
lists, and there are also your own
internal lists of people who have asked
not to be contacted.
Check against them before reaching out
and honor every opt out quickly.
Keep a record of the date and what was
done.
Fourth, state rules and industry rules.
Calling hours, licensing requirements,
and what you're allowed to say in
advertising can differ from state to
state and by industry.
Insurance, lending, and health are
especially closely regulated. And if
you're moving into a new vertical or a
new state, treat that as a reason to
stop and check, not just to assume.
Now a word on responsibility.
If you work through a network, the
network will often set the compliance
rules for its publishers and
advertisers.
If you work directly with a partner,
there's no network doing that for you.

your responsibility.

responsibility for their commercial
relationships.
So make sure your written agreement
spells out who is responsible for what.
Here are three key takeaways from this
lesson.
Number one, consent must be documented
and tied to the specific seller.
If you can't show who agreed, when, and
to what, assume you can't prove it.
Number two, make recording disclosures
and suppression checks a standard part
of every setup.
When it's a routine setup, it never gets
forgotten. Number three, when you're
unsure, pause the campaign and ask your
compliance contact.
Pausing to ask is always cheaper than
fixing a violation afterwards. And one
last reminder, this was general
education, not legal advice. So please
confirm the current rules for your
situation. In the next episode, we turn
to the people side of the business,
working with publishers.

My Story:
In 2022, I became a licensed insurance agent, struggling just like most. I used my mom's credit card to buy leads — I didn't have any money. I made a few sales but nothing crazy, averaging around $5k–$10k for three months. Then I invested in learning how to run my own ads, and everything changed. I started averaging $30k months, one month hitting $80k. That's when I saw the bigger picture — the real money wasn't in chasing leads; it was in owning them.

What I Do Now:
I built AgentCalls, a Pay Per Call brokerage that does over six figures every single month, selling leads and calls to insurance agents. I cracked the system, built the relationships, and turned it into a real business that prints whether I'm working or not.
Now I teach everyday people how to start and scale their own Pay Per Call and Pay Per Lead business through Middleman Mafia. No hard selling, no cold calling, no experience needed. You can learn how to do the exact same thing across any niche.

Results vary. Nothing here is a guarantee of income.

तो ये सारी चीजों के ऊपर आपको सही ढंग से देखना पड़ेगा। आपको नंबर ऑफ बिड के ऊपर बहुत ज्यादा फोकस करना पड़ेगा। देन यू विल नो कहां पे ऐड चलाना है, कहां पे ऐड नहीं चलाना है। इसके अलावा जो अगली चीज होती है जिसके ऊपर सबसे ज्यादा फोकस हम लोग जब भी किसी भी स्टूडेंट को सिखाते हैं तो हम सबसे ज्यादा फोकस करते हैं वो करते हैं नेगेटिव कीवर्ड लिस्ट पे। नेगेटिव कीवर्ड लिस्ट के ऊपर आपको बहुत ज्यादा फोकस करना है। अगर आप नेगेटिव कीवर्ड लिस्ट के ऊपर फोकस नहीं कर रहे हो देन आप यकीन मान के चलिए आप बहुत ज्यादा लॉस खा जाओगे। बहुत ज्यादा लॉस खा जाओगे। अब यहां पे भी ना कि बड अमाउंट में इसको भी आप कम करके जैसे मैं यहां पे आपको दिखाता हूं यहां पे $20 करता हूं। अब यहां पे जो जिप होंगे ना हमारे बहुत कम जिप हो जाएंगे। ठीक है? एक से नहीं हो रहा है। तो इस तरीके से हम लोग ना कुछ थोड़ा सा दिमाग लगाते हो और bिडमप का सही से यूज़ करते हैं। और जब आप जिस दिन आपने bitmap का यूज़ सही से करना चालू कर दिया कहीं ना कहीं आप पेपर कॉल में अपनी प्रॉफिटेबिलिटी निकालना चालू कर दोगे। ठीक है? तो ये पूरा का पूरा सिनेरियो था। इस वीडियो के थ्रू मैं ये आपको सिखाना मैं चाहता था। ठीक है? साथ ही साथ नेगेटिव कीवर्ड लिस्ट के ऊपर एक मैं बहुत ही डेडिकेटेड वीडियो बनाने वाला हूं। तो वहां पे भी आपको बहुत कुछ सीखने को मिलेगा। सो आई होप कि आपको समझ में आया होगा कि क्या चीज एग्जैक्टली मैं बताना चाहता हूं। आई होप आपको अगर थोड़ी सी भी इंफॉर्मेशनेशन अच्छी लगी हो तो चैनल को सब्सक्राइब करना, वीडियो को लाइक करना और शेयर जरूर करना। सो और जिसको भी चीजों के बारे में कांटेक्ट करना हो बहुत सारी चीजें मेरे से पूछनी हो दे कैन दे हैव माय WhatsApp नंबर दे कैन कांटेक्ट मी। सो आई होप यू लाइक दिस वीडियो। थैंक यू। थैंक यू वेरी मच।

metadata.shortDescription:
the biggest challenge on both ends of the spectrum seems to boil down to maintaining longevity in campaigns, While some exceptional cases may see campaigns lasting several months, it's not the norm. The key to success lies in establishing a constant feedback loop with clients. This feedback loop is crucial because what works today might not work tomorrow, as seen with Facebook advertising becoming more saturated and costly.

Another challenge is account management. While many affiliates and media buyers excel at driving online traffic, they may lack skills in client management and understanding client needs. This disparity can hinder their ability to scale effectively.

metadata.title: How to Read a Pay Per Call Campaign Before You Send Traffic | Pay Per Call University #6
metadata.author: ExclusiveLiveCall
metadata.shortDescription:
A Pay Per Call campaign says $300 per call.
Sounds great — but does that actually mean you'll make $300?
Not necessarily.
In Episode 6 of Pay Per Call University, I break down exactly how to read a Pay Per Call campaign before you spend money or send traffic.
The payout is only one piece of the equation. You need to understand the complete campaign rules and how those rules affect your ability to actually get paid.
In this episode, you'll learn:
- Payout vs. the actual billable event
- Geographic coverage — states, cities, ZIP codes and service areas
- Campaign schedules and operating hours
- Qualification requirements
- Allowed and restricted traffic sources
- Call-duration requirements
- How AI Verdict™ can add another layer beyond duration
- Daily call caps
- Buyer concurrency
- Duplicate-call rules
- Buyer priority and routing
- Why the highest-paying buyer isn't always the buyer that receives the call
- What happens when a buyer reaches their cap or can't answer
- How multiple buyers can improve monetization
- How otherwise lost calls can potentially be recovered
We also show how these concepts connect to ProAxis.ai.
Traditional call-tracking platforms can help you track and route calls. With ProAxis, our goal is to take that further by bringing together campaign management, intelligent routing, AI conversation analysis, publishers, buyers, leads, appointments, billing, and Call Recovery within one platform.
For example, what happens when you generate a legitimate consumer but no buyer is available for that ZIP code?
Instead of automatically treating that opportunity as worthless, ProAxis Call Recovery is designed to help preserve the consumer intent and potentially turn the opportunity into a lead, appointment, or another valid monetization path.
That's an important concept for publishers:
Making more money doesn't always require generating more traffic. Sometimes you need better technology to monetize more of the traffic you're already generating.
Pay Per Call University is completely free. My goal is to teach you how the Pay Per Call industry actually works—from publishers and buyers to campaigns, routing, AI, billing, and building your own network.
🌐 ProAxis.ai
Key lesson from Episode 6:
Don't choose a campaign based only on the payout. Understand the rules that determine whether you actually get paid.
#PayPerCall #PayPerCallUniversity #ProAxis #LeadGeneration #PerformanceMarketing #AffiliateMarketing #CallTracking #CallRouting #AI #DigitalMarketing

segments.text: Welcome back to Papercall University.
Today, we're going to talk about one of
the biggest mistakes new publishers
make. They open a campaign and
immediately look at one number, the
payout. Roofing, $300. Water damage,
$1,000. Legal, maybe hundreds or even
thousands of dollars depending on the
campaign. And they think, "This is
amazing. I just need to generate calls."
Not so fast. Before you send a single
call, you need to understand exactly
what the campaign accepts. What
locations, what schedule, what type of
caller, what services, what traffic
sources, what qualification
requirements. What's the billable event?
Are there caps? Are there duplicate
rules? Because a $300 campaign isn't
worth much to you if most of your
traffic doesn't qualify.
In this episode, I'm going to show you
how to read a Papercall campaign from
top-to-bottom and how technology can
automatically enforce many of these
rules before the call ever reaches the
buyer.
Think of a Papercall campaign as a set
of instructions. The campaign tells you
what the buyer wants, where they want
it, when they want it, how much they're
willing to pay, and what has to happen
before you get paid.
A typical campaign might include
campaign name, vertical, payout,
billable event, geographic coverage,
schedule, qualification requirements,
traffic source restrictions, call
duration or AI qualification rules,
daily caps, concurrency, duplicate
rules, and routing requirements. Every
one of these settings can affect whether
your call makes money. So, let's break
them down.
The first thing I want to look at is not
just the payout. I want to know what
triggers the payout. We learned this in
episode 5. Maybe it's a qualified call.
Maybe it's CPQ. Maybe it's an
appointment. Maybe it's an acquisition.
Maybe it's a sale. Imagine two
campaigns. Campaign A pays $150 for a
qualified call. Campaign B pays $800 for
an acquisition. You cannot compare those
numbers directly. The $800 campaign may
require you to generate many
opportunities before one acquisition
occurs. Always read the payout together
with the billable event. Those two
numbers belong together.
Next, where does the buyer actually want
calls? A campaign might be nationwide.
It might accept only certain states. It
could target specific cities. Or it
could go all the way down to individual
zip codes. This matters enormously.
Imagine you're generating plumbing calls
nationwide, but one buyer only covers
South Florida. A customer calls from
Dallas. Great consumer, great intent,
wrong geography.
If that's your only buyer, you may have
nowhere to send that call. This is why
publishers want broad coverage. And it's
why networks often combine multiple
buyers to create larger geographic
footprints.
In ProNexus.ai,
routing can use geographic information
such as zip code, state, and campaign
coverage to determine which eligible
buyer can receive the opportunity.
Instead of the publisher manually
figuring out where every call should go,
the routing technology can make that
decision dynamically.
Geography isn't the only thing that
matters. Time matters, too.
Maybe a buyer accepts calls Monday
through Friday from 9:00 to 5:00.
But your website doesn't stop generating
traffic at 5:00. Customers search at
night. They search on weekends. They
call whenever they need help. So, what
happens when the buyer is closed? A
basic setup might simply reject the
call. But that opportunity still has
value. A better system can look for
another available buyer. And if no live
buyer is available, technology can
potentially capture the consumer's
information, schedule an appointment, or
convert that opportunity into another
monetizable event.
This is something we focus heavily on
inside ProNexus.ai.
Don't automatically assume an unanswered
or unroutable call has zero value.
There may be another way to monetize the
opportunity.
Now, let's look at qualification
requirements. This is where campaigns
can become very different, even inside
the same vertical.
Two roofing buyers might both purchase
roofing calls, but want completely
different customers. One may accept roof
repair and replacement. Another may want
replacement only. One might accept
homeowners and commercial properties.
Another might require residential
homeowners. One may have additional
requirements around the project. This is
why you need to read every qualification
rule carefully. And once again, AI can
help. In ProNexus, conversational AI can
analyze what the caller actually says
and compare those signals against the
campaign requirements. Instead of
looking only at call duration, we're
trying to understand, did this caller
actually meet the requirements of this
specific campaign? Here's one publishers
sometimes overlook.
What traffic sources does the campaign
allow?
A buyer may accept Google search, SEO,
organic websites, certain paid media, or
approved publisher sources.
But they may restrict other sources.
Some buyers may not accept traffic from
Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace,
incentivized traffic, or certain call
center models.
That doesn't necessarily mean a traffic
source is universally bad. It means the
buyer decides what they're willing to
purchase. This is exactly why we talked
earlier about sub IDs and separate
tracking numbers. If you have five
traffic sources, don't throw all five
into one bucket. Track them separately.
In ProAcsys, the goal is to let networks
identify those sources and use that
information when determining which
campaigns and buyers are eligible for
the call. That protects your good
traffic when one source has a problem.
Next, you'll often see something like 60
seconds, 90 seconds, 120 seconds.
That's the traditional call duration
requirement we discussed in episode 4.
But now you know why duration alone can
be imperfect. A legitimate customer
might complete the important part of the
conversation in 70 seconds. Another
caller might stay connected for 4
minutes without meeting the campaign
requirements. That's why in proacsys.ai,
we designed AI Verdict Trademark to add
another layer of intelligence.
The system can analyze the conversation
against the campaign's rules.
Was there legitimate intent? Was the
requested service correct? Did the
caller appear to meet the qualification
requirements? What actually happened?
Duration is still useful,
but now we can combine the clock with an
understanding of the conversation.
Now let's talk about caps. A buyer might
say, "I want 20 calls per day." Once
they receive 20, they're done. That's
the daily cap.
Here's the problem for a publisher. Your
traffic doesn't necessarily stop when
the buyer reaches their cap. Your ads
are still running. Your websites are
still ranking. Customers are still
calling.
This is another reason having multiple
buyers is so important. If buyer A
reaches their cap, the routing system
should be able to look for buyer B, then
buyer C, then another eligible
destination.
The more coverage and buyer depth you
have, the better chance you have of
monetizing the traffic you're already
generating.
This is one of the major advantages of
building a network rather than depending
on a single buyer.
There's another campaign setting
beginners often don't understand,
concurrency.
Concurrency means how many calls a buyer
can handle at the same time. Imagine a
buyer says, "I can accept 50 calls per
day." That sounds great. But they only
have two agents answering phones. If
five calls arrive simultaneously, they
may not be able to handle all five.
That's where concurrency limits become
important. Maybe that buyer can receive
only two active calls at a time.
When those lines are occupied, new calls
need another destination.
A routing platform like ProNexus can
consider availability and routing rules
before determining where the next call
should go. Because sending a valuable
call to someone who can't answer it
doesn't help the publisher, the buyer,
or the customer.
Next, duplicates. Suppose the same
customer calls today and then calls
again tomorrow. Should the buyer pay
twice? Maybe. Maybe not. That's
determined by the campaign's duplicate
rules. A campaign might define a
duplicate window such as 7 days, 14
days, 30 days, or another period. So,
when you see a campaign payout, check
the duplicate policy. This can
materially affect your revenue. And
technology can automatically compare the
caller against previous activity instead
of expecting somebody to manually
inspect thousands of calls. Again,
campaign rules aren't just text on a
page. They should become logic inside
the platform.
Now things get really interesting.
Imagine you have three buyers that can
all accept the same roofing call.
Buyer A pays $150.
Buyer B pays 200. Buyer C pays 250.
Should you always send the call to buyer
C? Not necessarily. Maybe buyer C
doesn't cover that zip code. Maybe
they've reached their daily cap. Maybe
they're currently at maximum
concurrency. Maybe they don't accept
that traffic source. Maybe they're
closed. So, routing isn't simply who
pays the most. It's who is eligible to
receive this specific call right now.
And among those eligible destinations,
which routing logic should apply?
That's what modern pay-per-call
technology is designed to solve. In Pro
Axess, the goal is to evaluate those
conditions automatically and route each
opportunity according to the campaign
and buyer rules. Now, here's something
I'm particularly passionate about. What
happens when nobody can take the call?
Traditional thinking says, "No buyer, no
revenue, dead call."
But think about what you actually have.
You may have a real consumer, a real
phone number, a service they're looking
for, geographic information, and strong
purchase intent.
Why should that opportunity simply
disappear? Inside Pro Axess.ai,
we're building around the idea that an
unroutable or unanswered call can
potentially be recovered.
The system can capture the available
information, use AI to understand what
the consumer needs, and depending on the
setup, turn that opportunity into a
lead, an appointment, or another
monetizable event.
We call this concept call recovery
because publishers already paid to
create that opportunity. If technology
can recover even a percentage of those
otherwise lost calls, that can directly
improve publisher economics.
Now, let's put everything together.
When you're creating or evaluating a
campaign, don't think of it as simply
roofing $200. Think about the complete
rule set. What event triggers payment?
What geography is accepted? What
schedule? What qualifications? Which
traffic sources? What duration or AI
verification rules, what daily cap, what
concurrency, what duplicate window.
Which buyers can receive the traffic?
And what happens if the first buyer
can't take the call?
In a basic call tracking system, many of
these pieces may need to be configured
and managed separately. What we're
building with ProAxi.ai
is a system where these campaign rules
can work together across tracking,
routing, AI analysis, publishers,
buyers, leads, appointments, and
billing. Because every additional
opportunity you successfully route or
recover can potentially mean more
revenue from traffic you've already
generated.
So, here's the lesson I want you to
remember from episode six.
Never choose a campaign based only on
the payout. A $300 payout with poor
coverage, restrictive qualifications,
limited hours, and low buyer capacity
might be less profitable for your
traffic than a lower paying campaign
with excellent coverage and strong
availability. Read the entire campaign.
Understand the billable event.
Understand the geography. Understand the
traffic restrictions. Understand the
caps. Understand the routing. And most
importantly, understand what happens to
your traffic when the perfect buyer
isn't available. That's one of the
reasons we're building ProAxi.ai the way
we are. The goal isn't simply to track
calls. The goal is to help you monetize
more of the opportunities you're already
generating. Because in performance
marketing, improving your profit doesn't
always mean generating more traffic.
Sometimes it means losing less of the
traffic you already paid for. And in the
next episode, we're going to take the
next step and look at how calls are
actually routed between publishers,
networks, and buyers. And what happens
behind the scenes from the second the
customer dials the tracking number. I'll
see you in episode seven of Paper Call
University.
